sender: Priya Natarajan, Corporate Access, Halvorsen & Pike Securities
subject: Time-sensitive: call w/ former Apple iPhone ops director (now at Tier-1 camera module supplier) - Wed 8:00am ET
body:
Hi Ellen,

Flagging a small-group call we've arranged for tomorrow before our guest flies to Asia for supplier reviews. Only four slots; you were on the list given your AAPL interest.

Guest: Former Director of iPhone Operations at Apple (left 2023), currently SVP Customer Programs at a Tier-1 camera module supplier that ships into the iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max.

Why now: In our pre-screen she said her company received a revised December-quarter build signal last Thursday that is roughly 8-10% below the August plan on Pro Max camera modules, with the base model flat. Her read is that the reduction reflects sell-through in China and an inventory correction at carriers rather than component shortages. That runs counter to the Street view that Pro mix is driving higher December-quarter builds (consensus models ~84-86m units for the quarter).

Topics she has agreed to cover:
- Magnitude and timing of the revised forecast vs. prior cycles (she says 2022 is the closest analog)
- Whether other module/lens suppliers saw the same revision
- Pro vs. Pro Max mix and the folding device pull-in schedule
- What she would watch in Apple's guidance on the 29th

Logistics: Wednesday 8:00-8:45am ET, dial-in sent upon confirmation. Compliance pre-cleared; she will not discuss her current employer's non-public financials.

Please confirm by 6pm tonight so I can hold the slot.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Corporate Access | Halvorsen & Pike Securities
+1 212 555 0148
reason: Credible, time-sensitive access to a supply-chain insider whose firm reportedly received a lower December-quarter iPhone build forecast, which contradicts consensus expectations for higher builds. Taking the call could directly change AAPL positioning ahead of earnings.

subject: Transcript: Former hyperscaler network procurement lead on AI fabric choices (Spectrum-X vs. Ethernet merchant silicon)
body:
ATLAS INSIGHT CALLS | Transcript Summary | Call date: Oct 9, 2026

Expert: Former Director, Network Infrastructure Procurement at a top-3 U.S. hyperscaler (left June 2026). 11 years in role.
Interviewer: Atlas client (buy-side)

Key takeaways (summary prepared by Atlas; full transcript attached):

1. Networking choice for the next build. The expert said their former employer's 2027 AI cluster program has "standardized" on merchant-silicon Ethernet switches with in-house NICs for scale-out, after running Spectrum-X in two earlier clusters. Nvidia's NVLink remains the scale-up fabric inside racks.

2. Why the switch. Mainly cost and multi-vendor flexibility. "Spectrum-X performed well, but procurement wanted two sources and the merchant option closed the performance gap on collective operations with the last software release."

3. Scale. The 2027 program is "several hundred thousand accelerators," a mix of Nvidia GPUs and the hyperscaler's own chips. The expert estimated Nvidia's networking content per GPU in that program would fall by roughly 60-70% vs. the prior cluster.

4. Is this widespread? The expert believes at least one other hyperscaler is evaluating the same approach, but noted that neoclouds and sovereign buyers "still overwhelmingly take the full Nvidia stack."

5. Interviewer note: The expert was firm on the architecture decision, less sure on volumes.

Compliance: Expert affirmed no MNPI and no confidentiality obligations breached.

Full transcript (14 pages) attached. Reply to schedule a follow-up with this expert.
reason: An expert says a large hyperscaler's next AI cluster build will standardize on merchant Ethernet switching instead of Nvidia's Spectrum-X, which challenges the networking-attach assumption in long NVDA positions. Its importance depends on how much the desk's thesis relies on networking growth.
angle: value depends on the desk's existing exposure

subject: Sandridge AM: Recap of UK cloud market decision; MSFT impact limited
body:
SANDRIDGE PARTNERS | MORNING NOTE | Oct 13

MSFT - UK cloud decision recap (published yesterday)

For those who missed yesterday's coverage: the UK competition regulator published its final decision in the cloud services market investigation. Key points, all public:

- The regulator recommended "strategic market status" designations for the two largest cloud providers, opening the door to conduct requirements.
- Software licensing practices, including pricing for running Windows Server and SQL Server on rival clouds, were flagged as a priority area.
- Egress fees were addressed through voluntary commitments already announced by the providers.

Our take (unchanged): The UK accounts for low-single-digit percent of Microsoft's commercial cloud revenue. Any remedies would take 12-18 months to design. We see limited near-term financial impact, as we've written since the provisional findings.

Other items:
- No change to our MSFT estimates or Buy rating.
- Reminder: MSFT reports Oct 28.

Sandridge Partners Equity Research
reason: Recaps a UK regulator's cloud market decision that was published and widely covered yesterday. Restates the known conclusion that the near-term impact on Microsoft is limited.
angle: recap of a public earnings call or event

sender: Ruth Delacroix, Transportation Analyst, Tidewell Securities
subject: Rails: Labor talks enter mediation - what a 30-day cooling-off period means for Q4 volumes
body:
Tidewell Securities | Transportation | Industry Update

Rail labor: national bargaining moves to mediation

Talks between the national carriers' conference and a coalition of seven unions moved into federal mediation yesterday after the parties failed to agree on crew-consist language and wage step-ups for 2027-2029.

What happens next:
- Mediation typically lasts 60-120 days; a release from mediation triggers a 30-day cooling-off period.
- Any work stoppage before Q2 2027 looks very unlikely under that timeline.
- Historically, Congress has intervened in the two most recent national stoppage threats.

Volume implications: We model Q4 carload growth of +1.5% y/y and intermodal of +4.0% y/y. A protracted dispute would mainly affect shipper behavior in early 2027, with some intermodal shifting to truckload. Chemicals and grain shippers are most exposed.

Wage math: The unions' ask implies 4.5% annual increases vs. the carriers' 3.25% offer. Each 1 point of wage inflation is worth roughly 30-40bp of operating ratio for the large Class I carriers in our coverage.

Ratings unchanged. We continue to prefer the western carriers on pricing and intermodal exposure.

Ruth Delacroix | Tidewell Securities
Disclosures available on request.
reason: Well-researched note on rail labor mediation and freight volumes with no connection to the target technology companies. Outside the desk's coverage.
